directive:
Use the following verbatim `d0_directive`:

> Repair `lem:fixed-strata-central-limit` as a paper-owned result. In `core.json`, delete the entire mismatched `source` object attached to this node, change `"status": "cited"` to `"status": "proved"`, and add the proof below as `proof_tex`. In `writeup.tex`, insert the same proof immediately after the lemma. Do not add a replacement citation or theorem-level attestation.
>
> Preserve the lemma statement. Its normalization and covariance are correct. For formal precision, interpret “independent sampling across cohorts” as mutual independence of the finite collection of cohort-sample sigma-fields. The displayed `ass:cross-cohort-independence` currently uses pairwise notation; minimally clarify it to say that
> \[
> \bigl\{\sigma(Y_{gi}:1\le i\le n_g):g\in C\bigr\}
> \quad\text{are mutually independent}.
> \]
> Mirror that wording in the shorthand descriptions of \(\mathcal M_4\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{bd}}\). Pairwise independence alone is not generally enough to factor the joint characteristic function. This is a clarification of the intended independent-strata design, not a change to the substantive model.
>
> Insert this proof:
>
> ```tex
> \begin{proof}
> Write
> \[
> \widetilde{\overline Y}
> =\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(\overline Y_g),
> \qquad
> \widetilde m=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(m_g),
> \]
> in cohort-major order, and define
> \[
> W_{gN}
> =\frac1{\sqrt{n_g}}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}(Y_{gi}-m_g),
> \qquad
> W_N=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(W_{gN}).
> \tag{1}
> \]
> Since \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\), every \(n_g\to\infty\). For an arbitrary
> block vector \(a=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(a_g)\), the scalar
> i.i.d. central limit theorem, finite second moments, and mutual
> independence of the cohort samples give
> \[
> \begin{aligned}
> \mathbb E\exp\{it\,a^\prime W_N\}
> &=\prod_{g\in C}
> \mathbb E\exp\{it\,a_g^\prime W_{gN}\}\\
> &\longrightarrow
> \prod_{g\in C}
> \exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2}a_g^\prime\Sigma_ga_g\right\}\\
> &=\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2}
> a^\prime\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g)a\right\}.
> \end{aligned}
> \tag{2}
> \]
> Hence, by the Cramér--Wold device,
> \[
> W_N\Rightarrow
> \mathcal N\!\left(
> 0,\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g)
> \right).
> \tag{3}
> \]
> This conclusion remains valid when some \(\Sigma_g\) are singular;
> the corresponding Gaussian law is then degenerate.
>
> Let
> \[
> D_N=\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}
> \left(\sqrt{\frac N{n_g}}\,I_T\right),
> \qquad
> D=\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}
> \left(p_g^{-1/2}I_T\right).
> \tag{4}
> \]
> Share convergence gives \(D_N\to D\), while
> \[
> \sqrt N(\widetilde{\overline Y}-\widetilde m)=D_NW_N.
> \tag{5}
> \]
> Slutsky's theorem therefore yields
> \[
> \sqrt N(\widetilde{\overline Y}-\widetilde m)
> \Rightarrow
> \mathcal N\!\left(
> 0,\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g/p_g)
> \right).
> \tag{6}
> \]
> Finally, the untreated--treated ordering is obtained from the
> cohort-major ordering by the fixed stacking matrix \(\Pi\):
> \[
> \sqrt N(\overline Y-m)
> =\Pi\sqrt N(\widetilde{\overline Y}-\widetilde m).
> \tag{7}
> \]
> Applying the continuous mapping theorem to (6) proves
> \[
> \sqrt N(\overline Y-m)
> \Rightarrow
> \mathcal N(0,\Omega),
> \qquad
> \Omega
> =\Pi\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}
> (\Sigma_g/p_g)\Pi^\prime.
> \]
> \end{proof}
> ```
>
> Finite second moments are exactly sufficient for this lemma; the maintained finite-fourth-moment assumption is stronger and is needed elsewhere for covariance estimation. Covariance nonsingularity is unnecessary for the CLT itself, although `ass:covariance-interior` makes \(\Omega\) positive definite for downstream inversions.
>
> No downstream theorem statement or substantive prose requires revision. The proof supplies precisely the \(O_P(N^{-1/2})\) and Gaussian claims used by `lem:cohort-mean-ppml-linearization`, `thm:efficient-attainment`, and `thm:pointwise-wald-inference`. In the attainment proof, equation (7) is also correctly scaled: with \(\widehat p_g=n_g/N\), replacing \(1/\widehat p_g\) by \(1/p_g\) contributes
> \[
> \sum_{g\in C}
> (\widehat p_g^{-1}-p_g^{-1})
> N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
> h_g^{\star\prime}(Y_{gi}-m_g)
> =o_P(1),
> \]
> because \(C\) is finite, each normalized sum is \(O_P(1)\), and
> \(\widehat p_g^{-1}-p_g^{-1}=o(1)\). The fixed stacking map \(\Pi\)
> also introduces no scaling: it only reorders/selects the complete
> \(U\)-then-\(D\) stack.
